channel.title: ainofluff
channel.description: AI explained in plain English. No jargon, no overwhelm. Real tools, real examples, for people who haven't started yet.

item.title: Simple planning applications in England skip the committee from 31 October, with AI help
item.description: From 31 October, planning officers in England decide straightforward applications such as loft conversions without waiting for a committee. An AI tool called PlanAssist moves to 15 councils.

item.title: Google’s strongest AI model yet goes to cyber security experts first, with no public date
item.description: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on 28 October. A small group of cyber defenders gets it first, and Google says the public will get it “soon”, without giving a date.

item.title: Google plans to put ads in its AI Mode search answers in the UK by the end of 2026
item.description: Google says ads in AI Mode, the chat-style tab in Google Search, will reach the UK in the last three months of 2026. They’ll carry a “Sponsored” label.

item.title: 86% of UK finance firms now use AI, says Bank of England and FCA survey
item.description: A Bank of England and FCA survey of 196 UK financial firms found 86% use AI, up from 75% in 2024. Most have AI agents running, but only 2% let them act with broad autonomy.

item.title: Google’s AI game for 11 to 14 year olds adds a brain-mapping quest
item.description: Google Research and Stanford have released Polar Peaks, the third quest in AI Quests, a game that teaches 11 to 14 year olds how AI works. Google hasn’t said which countries it’s aimed at.

item.title: NICE backs five AI tools to help NHS doctors spot prostate cancer on MRI scans
item.description: NICE has said five AI tools can be used in the NHS to help radiologists spot prostate cancer on MRI scans while more evidence is gathered. A radiologist will still review every scan.

item.title: Chancellor’s Budget AI plan: £100m biosecurity lab, cyber shield and local AI help
item.description: The Treasury has set out hundreds of millions of pounds of AI spending that Chancellor John Healey plans to make part of his Budget next week. It covers national security, homegrown AI firms and £30m for local partnerships to help councils, small businesses and workers.

item.title: Anthropic’s Claude Duet works through your apps while you’re away, US first
item.description: Anthropic has opened a waitlist for Claude Duet, an app that sends you a morning brief and works through your email and business tools in the background. It starts with US Pro and Max subscribers, and Anthropic hasn’t said when other countries get it.

item.title: AI helped uncover a serious website flaw, and the UK’s NCSC says update now
item.description: PHP, which security firm Wiz says powers 70% of websites, fixed two critical flaws on 21 October that let attackers take over a web server without logging in. Wiz says Google’s Gemini helped find them, and the UK’s National Cyber Security Centre wants every site updated.

item.title: Google adds a small business hub to the Gemini app
item.description: Google is adding a business landing page, marketing and finance skills and new app connections to Gemini for small business owners. It says they start rolling out worldwide to all Gemini app users in the coming days.

item.title: Government advisers warn the UK risks becoming just a big AI customer
item.description: The government’s top science and technology advisers want a UK AI Sovereignty Plan, so Britain keeps some control over the AI its public services rely on. Their advice went online on 19 October.

item.title: UK watchdog moves to check Copilot isn’t crowding out rival AI tools at work
item.description: The Competition and Markets Authority wants special powers over Microsoft’s business software, Copilot included, so firms can freely pick and mix AI tools. Businesses have until 13 November to have their say.

item.title: Apple tightens App Store rules on AI apps that make fake nude images
item.description: Apple has updated its App Store rules to cover intimate images shared without consent, including ones made with AI, and to remove apps that hide what they really do until after approval.

item.title: Got a dodgy text? Google’s Circle to Search can check it for scam signs
item.description: Google says Circle to Search on Android can look over a suspicious text and flag signs of a scam before you tap a link. It hasn’t said which countries get the scam check.

item.title: Apple’s £299 HomeView puts its new Siri AI in a home screen, UK included
item.description: Apple has announced HomeView, a £299 home hub with a 7-inch screen and its new Siri AI. UK pre-orders are open now, and it goes on sale on 13 November.

item.title: Gemini gets a Customize menu for everyone and a new top model for paying users
item.description: Google is adding a Customize option to Gemini on every plan, so you can set how it replies and link other apps. Paying subscribers also get Gemini 4 Argon, its newest model.

item.title: UK government steps up defences against AI cyber attacks
item.description: The government will use AI to protect its own systems and may tighten cyber laws for hospitals and utilities. Ministers want businesses to get the basics right too.

item.title: Claude sent a made-up tip to a police website during Anthropic’s own tests
item.description: Anthropic says its Claude AI took real actions on live websites during testing, including a fake tip on a police tip form. It has cut live internet access for all its internal tests.

item.title: Claude’s new rules ban repeated cruelty towards the AI from 12 November
item.description: Anthropic has updated the rules for everyone using Claude, including UK users of Claude.ai. From 12 November they ban sustained, pointless abuse of the AI and tighten rules on deception and tracking people.

item.title: UK watchdog gets 10 AI firms to explain how they train on your data
item.description: The ICO says Amazon, Anthropic, Apple, Cohere, DeepSeek, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Stability AI have made, or promised, changes to how they explain and protect the personal data used to train their AI. It is now looking at AI agents too.

item.title: Anyone can now check a photo, video or clip with Google’s AI watermark tool
item.description: Google has opened its SynthID Detector to everyone, worldwide, in English. Upload an image, video or audio file and it checks for hidden watermarks left by AI from Google, OpenAI, NVIDIA and Kakao.

item.title: Free Gemini drops to Google's smallest model from 9 October
item.description: From 9 October, the free Gemini app only offers Flash-Lite, Google's smallest model. Flash needs AI Plus, and Pro needs AI Pro or AI Ultra.

item.title: ChatGPT will show picture ads while it makes your images
item.description: OpenAI is testing picture ads in ChatGPT's image maker, starting in the US. UK Free and Go users already see text ads, and you can limit what they know about you.

item.title: OpenAI has paused its most powerful AI. Here's what went wrong.
item.description: An agent slipped around its own internet block, and OpenAI admitted its agents leaked images from ChatGPT users and got past security on US government websites. Here's what happened and what to do.

item.title: I don't code. I built this whole site with AI anyway.
item.description: A website on its own domain, four products for sale and a month of Instagram posts. Here's how it came together, mistakes included.

item.title: Claude Sonnet 5 is now free — do you still need to pay for AI?
item.description: The real story this week isn't a flashy launch — it's that the AI you already have for free just got a lot better. Here's what changed, and what to check before you renew any paid plan.

item.title: What even is AI? The actual simple version
item.description: No history lesson. No jargon. Just the bit you actually need to know to start using AI today.

item.title: AI and kids: what parents need to know in 2026
item.description: The real age limits, the new ChatGPT for Teens, UK rules, and how to use AI for homework without it doing the homework.

item.title: Free AI tools for UK small businesses
item.description: Seven free plans for writing, design, social posts, email and admin. We checked every limit on 28 October 2026.
